# T006 — Repair Azure runtime dependency advisories

## Summary

Remediated the verified Azure XML, Speech WebSocket, JWT-signing, and UUID dependency findings in **both** npm locks without changing application source or wire/state behavior. Fresh scans on 2026-10-20 went from root **4 critical / 33 high / 11 moderate / 3 low** and backend **1 critical / 8 high / 4 moderate** to root **3 critical / 31 high / 7 moderate / 3 low** and backend **0 critical / 6 high / 0 moderate / 0 low**. Counts are affected package entries, not unique advisories.

## Changes

- `backend/package.json`: pin the first suitable direct releases of `@azure/identity` (4.13.1), Speech SDK (1.51.0), and `uuid` (11.1.1). Speech 1.51.0 declares patched `ws ^8.21.0` and `uuid ^11.1.1`; Identity 4.13.1 replaces the old MSAL 3/UUID 8 chain with MSAL 5. No ACS, Blob or communication client API changes.
- `package-lock.json`, `backend/package-lock.json`: npm-generated root and independent backend resolutions; `fast-xml-parser` 5.11.2 remains within `@azure/core-xml`'s `^5.0.7` constraint; `ws` 8.22.0, `jws` 4.0.1, and `uuid` 11.1.1 resolve the relevant advisories. npm also hoisted and deduplicated affected backend packages and resolved nearby transitive dependencies. No override or manual lock edit.

## Decisions

Scanned with the skill's native npm-audit wrapper before and after; traced root and standalone backend origins with `npm explain`, and checked first patched releases against the [GitHub Advisory Database API](https://api.github.com/advisories) on 2026-10-20. The old graph was `@azure/storage-blob → @azure/core-xml → fast-xml-parser`; `Speech SDK → ws, uuid`; `@azure/identity → @azure/msal-node → jsonwebtoken → jws` and old MSAL → uuid. The root frontend SWA CLI also consumes Identity but remains a separate delivery-tool family (T008). The critical/high XML parser issues require untrusted XML; XMLBuilder injection additionally requires attacker-controlled comments/CDATA. The Speech `ws` DoS requires a peer sending fragmented data; `jws` HMAC lookup exploit requires the vulnerable `createVerify` pattern, while its `jsonwebtoken` consumer uses `verify` per the advisory. Actual Azure input reachability is not proven by offline tests.

Node 24.21.0 / npm 11.19.0 were explicitly selected with `PATH=/opt/node/24/bin:$PATH`. Registry manifests show Identity 4.13.1 requires Node >=20, MSAL 5.6.0 >=20, core-xml 1.5.0 >=20, and Blob 12.29.1 >=20; Speech 1.51.0 advertises no Node engine restriction. Queried parent peerDependencies were empty, and clean `npm ci`, `npm ci --prefix backend`, and offline tests confirm installation under Node 24. npm chose later safe releases inside existing parent ranges, rather than an unnecessary direct override; the only major transitive changes are required by the patched Identity parent and passed offline boundary characterization.

## Validation

Run from repository root with `PATH=/opt/node/24/bin:$PATH` in each process; do **not** run root and backend clean installs concurrently, because they share a workspace directory. An initial simultaneous test/install collided on files under `backend/node_modules` and failed with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`; a sequential root `npm ci` and rerun restored all tests without source changes.
